newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to propose better gene-food labels.
newsitem.headline: Commission to propose better gene-food labels.

text.p: The European Commission will soon propose improved labelling of genetically modified food products, Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard said on Wednesday.
Bjerregaard was commenting after the Commission approved Ciba Geigy's application for market release of gene-modified maize in accordance with EU Directive 90/220.
"We must not miss this opportunity to repeat our clear signal that a better labelling is one of the ways forward in this area," Bjerregaard said in a statement.
"The Commission intends to deal further with this problem when a proposal - as soon as possible - will be put forward for revision of Directive 90/220," she added.
At present the directive does not allow obligatory labelling to show that a product is genetically modified without an assessment of the risk.
The Commission also recommended that the possibilities for labelling under a proposed EU Regulation on genetically modified and other novel foods should be considered.
The Commission said it recognised the need to increase public confidence and for more scientific research.
A new report on implementation of Directive 90/220 stressed the need to consider labelling rules for genetically modified food products.
The Commission said it welcomed a letter from Ciba Geigy on December 17 stating its readiness to cooperate on labelling.

"We would like to re-affirm our proposal to label the bags containing our seeds, indicating that the product has been obtained using biotechnology techniques," the Commission quoted Ciba Geigy as stating in the letter.

"We would also like to reiterate our readiness... to develop an insect resistance strategy and to implement monitoring of insect resistance in Europe, in order to safeguard any concerns which may have been raised," the letter added.
Ciba Geigy was not immediately available to comment on the letter.
